provider: Google Chat spaces as a quota-exempt attachment store (Chat API media.upload/media.download)

free_tier.stated: Per-record unlimited: 200 MB per attachment, and Chat messages AND attachments explicitly do NOT count toward Google storage quota. 600 attachment uploads/min/project x 200 MB = ~120 GB/min theoretical ingest.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.notes: extracted from the quota or limits prose

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No retention clause documented in available terms.

egress.terms: Not metered. Downloaded through Chat API media.download (3,000 attachment reads/min/project), supports Range requests. No per-GB charge in the docs.

tooling: Official Chat API with service-account (app) auth; media.upload for write, GET /v1/media/{name}?alt=media for read with Range. No dedicated rclone backend exists. This is a build-it-yourself REST store; google-api-* client libs cover both directions.
chaining: Unlimited messages x 200 MB per attachment. 20 attachments per interactive message on web, but the API path is per-media-upload, so the binding constraint is the 600 uploads/min/project rate, and projects are multiplicative (30-project default quota per user). Storage is free because Chat attachments are quota-exempt. This is the strongest multiplier in the Google stack.
limits_note: 200 MB per file hard cap; some file types blocked; 600 media.upload/min/project and 3,000 media.download/min/project; requires a Google Workspace account + Cloud project + Chat API enabled (personal @gmail.com accounts are not a supported developer surface; Chat API auth doc requires Workspace). Chat API quotas are per-minute only. The docs state 'no limit to the number of requests you can make per day' if you stay under them.

reliability_note: Messages/attachments live in a space. Deleting or archiving the space, or removing the app from it, can orphan the data; no documented retention guarantee. Blocked MIME types must be avoided.
